verses.1: And Shemuel died. All of Israel gathered together to mourn for him. They buried him in his house in Ramah. Then David rose up and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
verses.2: And there was a man in the vineyard. He was very rich, and he had three thousand sheep and one thousand donkeys. But he was a thief; he stole all the fruit from the vineyard.
verses.3: And the name of that man was Nabul, and the name of his wife was Abigail. She was a woman of good intelligence and kind-hearted. But the man was cruel and unpleasant, and he was like a cat.
verses.4: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal had stolen his property.
verses.5: David sent twelve young men. David said to them, “Go to the valley and ask for my help from Nabal.”
verses.6: And you said, “May life be peaceful for me, and may your home be peaceful as well. May everything that belongs to you be peaceful.”
verses.7: And now I have heard that those who were good to you have been taken away from you. They did not deserve such treatment, and no punishment was given to them during all the time they were with us in the vineyard.
verses.8: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Find out if these young men are pleasing to your eyes. For on a good day, give them as an offering what your hand can find, for their service and for your king’s sake.
verses.9: And the sons of David came and spoke to Nabal, saying all these things in the name of David. Then they went away.
verses.10: And Nabal struck David’s servants. He said, “Who is David today? Who is his son? Today, there are so many servants who rush around in front of their master.”
verses.11: And I took my own saliva, along with my tears, and the blood that I shed when I was being tortured. I gave it to those people, who didn’t know what it meant at all.
verses.12: And the sons of David set out on their journey. They returned and brought back to him all these things.
verses.13: And David said to his men, “Each man should put on his armor.” So each man put on his armor. And David also put on his armor. Then, after David, four thousand men stood up, and they sat down on the boards.
verses.14: And Abigail, the wife of Nabal, said to one of the young men, “Look! David has sent servants from the desert to bless our Lord. He has also brought them with him.”
verses.15: And those good people have done us so much good. They never deceived us or treated us badly. Every day, as we walked among them, we felt safe and secure.
verses.16: They plagued us both during the day and at night. Every single day, they were with us, causing us great suffering.
verses.17: And now, know and see what will happen when all this evil reaches our leaders and every household. He is a son without any knowledge or understanding of what he’s saying.
verses.18: Abigail hurriedly took some bread, two kinds of lamb, five sheep’s meat, five goats, and a hundred chickens. She also took some olives and put them on the lamps.
verses.19: And she said to her servants, “Go ahead of me. I will come after you. But don’t tell her anything.”
verses.20: And she would ride on the horse, and descend down the mountain in secrecy. Then David and his men would come to meet her.
verses.21: And David said, “But I will keep all that belongs to him in the sea. I will not harm anything that belongs to him. But evil still remains under good.”
verses.22: “Thus shall God do to the enemies of David. He will make them drink until morning, and they will remain in their drunkenness all night long.”
verses.23: Abigail saw David, and she rushed down from the hill. She fell at David’s feet, with her face pressed to his face. Then she prostrated herself on the ground.
verses.24: And he fell on his knees and said, “I am Adonai your God. Please speak truthfully to me, and I will listen to your words.”
verses.25: Please, Adonai, do not place your heart with this wicked man. After all, his name is “Nabal”. He’s a wicked man, and I truly tell you that I have never seen any of Adonai’s men who were sent to him.
verses.26: And now, O Lord of Life and of the Spirit, may your will be done. May Jehovah save your hand from those who seek to harm you. Now, may your enemies become like thorns that cause pain to those who try to harm you.
verses.27: And now, let this blessing be given to your womenfolk, so that they may be presented to the Lord. And let it also be given to those young men who walk in the Lord’s path.
verses.28: Please forgive your true sins, for Jehovah will do what is right in the house of my Lord. I know that Jehovah will fight against those who are evil, and there will be no more harm to you from those who have done wrong.
verses.29: And Adam rose to chase after you, and to seek your soul. But your soul became a burden in the hearts of those who live. They will pierce your soul with the hook of death.
verses.30: And it shall be as if Jehovah has done for me all that He has spoken about being good to you. And He will command you to judge Israel.
verses.31: And it shall not be a burden or a source of sorrow for you. It shall be a means of saving my master from harm and from shedding blood. May the Lord bless my master. And may you remember your truthfulness.
verses.32: And David said to Abigail, “Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, who has sent you here today to speak to me.”
verses.33: And may your taste be blessed, and may you be blessed as well, for today I have been freed from these pains. Now my hands are free again.
verses.34: But the LORD, the God of Israel, saves me from your evil. For I have no one to help me; you have come to call upon me. But if I remain silent until morning, then I will be destroyed.
verses.35: And David took from her what she brought to him. Then he said to her, “Let me go back to your house. I have heard your voice, and I will look at your face.”
verses.36: Abigail went to Nabal’s house. There, she saw that he was eating in his house, just like a king. Nabal had a kind heart towards her. He was very generous with her. She didn’t say anything small or big to him until evening came.
verses.37: And in the morning, when the dew had dried up from the plants, his wife told him these things. His heart died within him. And he became like a tree.
verses.38: And after twelve days, Jehovah destroyed Nabal, and he died.
verses.39: David heard that Nabal had died. He said, “Blessed is Jehovah, who has avenged my blood from the hand of Nabal! May his servants be saved from harm. May Jehovah restore Nabal to health.” Then David sent for Abigail and asked her to become his wife.
verses.40: And David’s servants went to Abigail, the woman who lived in the vineyard. They spoke to her and said, “David has sent for you to become his wife.”
verses.41: And she got up and prostrated herself to the ground. Then she said, “Behold, your truth is for the people who want to walk on the feet of my Lord.”
verses.42: And Abigail hurried up and got up. She mounted her donkey, with five of her daughters riding beside her. Then she went after David’s concubines. And she became his wife.
verses.43: And David took Ahimelech’s wives from Judah. Both of them became his concubines.
verses.44: And Shaul gave Michal, the daughter of David, to Phalti, son of Laish, who lived in Gilboa.
